details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:40-78 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The locally defined `_embed_input_file` is effectively unreachable when `gh_helpers.sh` sources successfully, so the UTF-8-safe truncation logic in this file never runs in the normal path.
  WHY: `command -v _embed_input_file` succeeds after sourcing the helper, so the guard skips the local implementation and the fallback only matters if helper sourcing fails.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:46-78 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The local fallback `_embed_input_file` does not implement the `diff` mode supported by `gh_helpers.sh`, so a future diff-mode call would be truncated as head mode and may emit a partial hunk.
  WHY: The fallback currently only handles the default path, so the behavior silently diverges if the helper cannot be sourced.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1192-1195 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Clearing `editor_refused.flag` without a defaulted `PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR` can turn the path into `/editor_refused.flag` when the variable is unset.
  WHY: The workflow normally sets the variable, but outside that context the unguarded expansion points at the filesystem root.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2204-2231 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: `_integration_branch_ahead_of_default` does not validate that the URI-encoded branch segment is non-empty before building the compare API URL.
  WHY: If `jq` fails or returns empty, the request is malformed and the compare lookup can fail unexpectedly.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1195-1196 | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The refusal regex uses redundant alternation for `can ?not` and `can.?t`, which adds maintenance noise without changing behavior.
  WHY: Both patterns match the same class of refusal text, so one is unnecessary.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5849-5868 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The managed-path stall-recovery review guard can race with a PR update because it consults cached run state before the later remote-head comparison.
  WHY: A workflow can start on the branch between those checks, letting the guard reason over stale state until the later fetch notices the head advanced.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5902-5908 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The standalone-path stall-recovery review guard has the same race window as the managed path.
  WHY: It uses the same cached workflow-run snapshot before the later remote-head recheck, so a new run can begin after the snapshot and before the fetch.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2233-2259 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: When compare-API lookup fails, the helper does not distinguish branch absence from API or parse failures in its error output.
  WHY: The same failure path is used for multiple causes, leaving operators without the specific reason.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:4984-5000 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The auto-merge guard can include unrelated retry stderr in its warning because it does not separate `gh_retry` diagnostics from the actual failure text.
  WHY: The step only checks whether the temp file exists, not whether stderr content is meaningful root-cause output.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2406-2420 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: Adding `integration_ahead_by` and `integration_contained_in_default` can break strict JSON consumers that reject unknown fields.
  WHY: The change is backward-compatible for normal parsers, but strict schema checks may fail on the expanded payload.
- probably_unnecessary_but_read_if_stuck.md:573-597 | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The rollback notes reference specific file locations that can drift after refactors.
  WHY: The instructions are informational, so code movement can make them stale without any runtime signal.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:1200-1210;1693-1703 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `ISSUE_NUMBER` is promoted into the workflow env without validation, so a failed or skipped create-issue step can leave downstream branch logic with an empty issue number.
  WHY: That can form `ai/issue-` and confuse later lookup/branch-matching logic.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5826-5932 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The retrigger-review in-flight guard uses `_rtr_head_sha` even though the surrounding code appears to define `_rtr_origin_head_sha`, which can break the head-sha match for blank `head_branch` workflow_dispatch runs.
  WHY: If the variable is empty, the jq fallback never matches on `head_sha`, weakening the guard against empty-commit pushes during an active review run.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7686-7769 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The standalone stall-recovery sweep may reuse `_STD_ITER_PR_NUM_CACHED` from a different issue context.
  WHY: Reusing a cached PR number without revalidating the issue→PR relationship can direct recovery actions at the wrong issue/PR pair.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2398-2432 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The `integration_contained_in_default` comparison is type-sensitive and treats integer `0` differently from string `"0"`.
  WHY: Real callers that pass an integer can be marked incomplete even when the branch is fully contained.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~line 5826 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: A checkout failure in managed-path retrigger_review now exits without issuing the operator notification that previously fired unconditionally.
  WHY: Because `tg_notify` only runs after `_rtr_push_succeeded="true"`, the failure path becomes silent and the stall is harder to diagnose.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~line 7686 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The standalone stall-recovery path has the same silent-failure gap on `git fetch` failure.
  WHY: The failure bypasses both the push-success branch and the linked-PR notification path, so no alert is emitted.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:389-392 | severity=high | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `RB_JUDGE_PR_DIFF_MAX_BYTES` can be set above Codex’s stdin limit, making the prompt oversize and causing every retry to fail before model execution.
  WHY: The current validation only enforces a positive integer, so an operator can choose a value that passes validation but still exceeds the hard cap once the other prompt sections are added.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:403-410 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The UTF-8-safe diff truncation loop can still cut a multibyte character mid-sequence in some cases.
  WHY: It only walks backward across continuation bytes and can stop at the cap even when the cap lands inside a multibyte code point.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:395 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The reported diff byte count can undercount because `printf '%s'` strips trailing newlines before `wc -c`.
  WHY: The truncation decision and the displayed size then use the same undercounted value, so the operator sees a smaller number than the original payload size.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:417 | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The truncation note hardcodes "1 MB cap" instead of tying the message to the configured max-bytes value.
  WHY: The log text can become misleading if the cap is changed later.
- tests/test_orchestrate_integration_ahead_by_gate.py:1-594 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The new test file uses tab indentation throughout and may fail the repo’s Python style checks.
  WHY: The rest of the test suite uses 4-space indentation, so this file is inconsistent with the established linting convention.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
